OccurrenceCleaner — Claude Code context

Source: CLAUDE.md

What it is

An R package that flags errors in species occurrence records (GBIF and similar) at any scale, from a data frame of a few thousand records to a whole GBIF snapshot of billions. It runs the record tests of CoordinateCleaner (Zizka et al. 2019, doi:10.1111/2041-210X.13152) with the same definitions and default buffers, computed as nearest-neighbour queries in C++ instead of per-record polygon buffers, and streams records from disk so memory does not bound the input.

It grows past CoordinateCleaner by adding tests of its own (duplicate definitions, stated coordinate uncertainty, record year, GBIF issue flags, habitat-aware sea test). Those are marked as additions and never change what a CoordinateCleaner-equivalent test returns.

Version 0.1.0 is built (2026-10-09). dev_notes/ holds the equivalence findings against CoordinateCleaner, the reference-data comparison and the benchmark table; read them before changing a test or a gazetteer.

Principles

  • The engine always returns flags. Every test writes one bit per record; the engine removes nothing and bakes in no threshold. A cleaning rule is a query over the flags, chosen afterwards. Removing records is an optional selection interface on top: keep_unflagged() after flagging, and the per-test cleaning functions clean_<test>(). Year and coordinate uncertainty stay raw columns and are cut at analysis time.
  • Equivalence is the trust argument. Each CoordinateCleaner-equivalent test has a test in tests/testthat/ that runs CoordinateCleaner itself on sampled records and requires identical flags (skip_if_not_installed("CoordinateCleaner")). A disagreement is a bug unless it is a documented, deliberate difference listed in the test file and in the help page of that test.
  • One front door for flagging. One flagging verb, flag_occurrences(), whose input can be a data frame or an on-disk table (vectra node / Parquet directory); the return follows the input. It is the interface for running tests together, keeping their results and processing large tables. Tests are chosen by an argument, not by separate flag_*() functions. A second verb tallies flags into loss tables.
  • Cleaning functions come from the registry. clean_<test>() exists for every test in .flag_layout, built by clean_fun() in R/clean.R: it runs flag_occurrences() on one test and drops what it flags, with the test’s buffer or .default_settings options as arguments. No test logic in a cleaning function; a new test gets its cleaning function as one line in R/clean.R, documented on the test’s help page (test-clean.R asserts one per test). Data frames only; a chain applies a grouped test to the records earlier steps kept.
  • Never export CoordinateCleaner’s cc_* names: that would mask its functions on attach.
  • Reference data is pinned and versioned. Every gazetteer the package uses carries its source, version and retrieval date, and the flag output records which reference version produced it.

Licence and dependencies

  • MIT. CoordinateCleaner is GPL-3, so nothing from it (code or its bundled data) is copied into this package. It is in Suggests only: used by the equivalence tests and by an explicit reference = "CoordinateCleaner" choice that reads its tables from the user’s own installation at run time. It also pulls 66 packages recursively, which is the second reason it is not in Imports.
  • Own reference data is built in data-raw/ from the original public sources that CoordinateCleaner itself draws on: Natural Earth (public domain) for land, countries, admin-1 units, populated places/capitals and urban areas; the institution gazetteer from GBIF’s GRSciColl bulk export, Wikidata, Wikipedia’s lists of natural history museums, GeoNames and BGCI GardenSearch (terms per source in dev_notes/reference_data.md).
  • Imports: vectra (>= 0.13.0) (CRAN, the user’s own C11 columnar engine; tbl_parquet() and collect_chunked() for streaming, write_vtr() for the flag parts) and Rcpp (kd-tree, geodesic and point-in-polygon core). Check the recursive footprint before adding anything else.

Prior implementation to port

The algorithm already ran over 2,460,201,588 GBIF records in the mountain-area-garcia project:

  • C:/GillesC/Documents/TaskGoblin/colabs/mountain-area-garcia/occurrences/clean/clean_tag.py (Python, numpy + scipy cKDTree): one uint16 per record, proximity tests as nearest-neighbour queries on the unit sphere (chord distance), gazetteers exported from CoordinateCleaner 3.0.1 by export_gazetteers.R in the same folder, radii asserted from gazetteers/cc_defaults.csv.
  • verify_clean.py (same folder) checks a tagged stream against its tally.
  • dev_notes/cleaning_rule_decision.md in that repo is the worked example of choosing a rule over the flags (nine rules from raw to strict).

Differences to fix in the port, not to carry over: the sea test there used that project’s own land mask, not Natural Earth land; there is no duplicate test; it was never checked record by record against CoordinateCleaner.

Consumer

The ali-filters collaboration (Ali Omar, same working group): a data paper on what the standard filters remove across taxonomic groups, record age and coordinate precision, run over the GBIF snapshot of 2026-10-01 at E:/research/raw/occurrences/gbif_snapshot/2026-10-01/. Project notes: C:/GillesC/Documents/TaskGoblin/colabs/ali-filters/. Version 0.1.0 is what gets shared with Ali.

Build and test

Windows R at C:/Program Files/R/R-4.6.1/bin/Rscript.exe. Write multi-line R to a .run*.R file (ignored by git and the build) rather than Rscript -e.

devtools::document()
devtools::test()
devtools::check(args = "--no-manual")

After any C++ change: Rcpp::compileAttributes() then devtools::document(). After a header-only change, delete src/*.o and src/*.so/*.dll before building, or nothing recompiles.

Conventions

  • Branch main, commit directly.
  • Roxygen and Rd text ASCII only.
  • CI workflows trigger on push, pull_request and workflow_dispatch; no schedule:.
  • Docs follow the house docs skills (docs-style with docs-readme or docs-articles); sidecars/ holds story, journey and information. Session handoff and the next docs tasks: dev_notes/current.md (local, git-ignored); decisions and lessons: dev_notes/docs_overhaul.md.
